title: Jacket potatoes with pulled pork and apple salad

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Pork, potatoes, yoghurt, cider vinegar, sugar and fresh produce are all ordinary home ingredients, with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every item, including boneless pork shoulder, is an everyday Tesco purchase at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only an oven, a roasting tray, foil, forks and a bowl, and slow-roasting and shredding are beginner-friendly.

works.reason: Covered pork at 150°C fan for 3 hours will shred, the potatoes will bake through in 1½ hours, and 800g pork with four potatoes suits four, though the leaves go undressed.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers rubbing the pork, oiling the potatoes, shredding and slicing, and 180 minutes matches the 3-hour roast.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, the names match their ids, and only water is added.

seasonal_feel.reason: The salad leaves are only tossed together 'to serve' beside a slow-roast pulled pork jacket potato, so the hero is a side garnish rather than the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Pork, jacket potatoes, yoghurt and a fresh apple and radish salad make a proper, appealing family meal.
